skill.name: asoscan-setup
skill.description: When the user wants to set up ASOScan, for example to connect the ASOScan plugin or connector in ChatGPT or Claude, get an API access key for a coding agent, set up webhooks (including Slack or Microsoft Teams alerts), or connect Google Play Console or App Store Connect. Also use when the user mentions "connect ASOScan", "connect my ASOScan account", "get my API key", "set up webhooks", "send alerts to Slack", "connect my Play Console", "connect my App Store account", or "how do I hook this up". Works with no account and no key.
skill.summary: Guides ASOScan account connections, API key setup, webhook configuration, and app store integrations.
skill.author: asoscan

security_audit.summary: Most alerts reflect Markdown formatting, documented setup commands, or legitimate authentication to ASOScan; no evidence found of prompt injection or unauthorized exfiltration. Five findings identify plaintext credential persistence through shell configuration or persistent environment settings. Webhook verification guidance also omits a timestamp freshness check, leaving replay prevention unspecified.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:63 recommends persisting an API key in a plaintext shell startup file.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the startup-file recommendation and prefer an operating system credential store or secret manager with narrowly scoped, temporary environment injection.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:66 and SKILL.md:69 persist API keys through fish universal variables and Windows user environment settings.
remediation.suggestion: Use session-only credentials by default, avoid literal secrets in shell history, and explain persistence risks before offering persistent alternatives.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:108-112 describes webhook HMAC verification without timestamp freshness validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require a bounded timestamp tolerance and constant-time signature comparison before processing events; reject duplicate deliveries when an event identifier is available.

content.user_title: Connect ASOScan Accounts and Configure Integrations
content.value_statement: ASOScan setup spans assistant connections, API credentials, webhook destinations, and app store permissions. This skill guides each setup path and explains verification steps and account restrictions.
actual_capabilities: Guides ASOScan assistant connections and documents Claude Code plugin installation commands.
Checks connected account usage through get_usage when the ASOScan tools are available.
Explains API key creation, permission choices, environment configuration, and usage endpoint verification.
Guides dashboard webhook setup for Signed JSON, Slack, and Microsoft Teams destinations.
Explains app store connection workflows and requires current official instructions for external setup steps.
Distinguishes authentication failures, plan restrictions, and features unavailable to an account.
limitations: Webhooks require dashboard configuration; the skill cannot register them through the public API.
API access, webhooks, and store connections depend on account plans or feature availability.
The package contains guidance, not a bundled verification script or webhook receiver implementation.
Ad account setup and publishing listing text to app stores are outside its scope.

use_cases.title: Connect an Assistant
use_cases.description: Choose an assistant connection path, authorize ASOScan access, and check remaining API credits when connected tools are available.

use_cases.title: Prepare Coding Agent Access
use_cases.description: Create an appropriately scoped API key, configure access locally, and distinguish authentication errors from plan restrictions.

use_cases.title: Configure Team Alerts
use_cases.description: Select webhook events and delivery formats, connect a Slack or Teams destination, and test delivery through the ASOScan dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Connection Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect my ASOScan account to Claude. Check whether ASOScan tools are available before asking me to create an API key.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up API Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating a read-only ASOScan API key for Codex. Keep credentials out of chat and use session-only secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Slack Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through ASOScan Slack webhook setup. Check current official Slack instructions, explain event selection, and show how to test delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Signed Event Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan ASOScan Signed JSON webhook setup for my HTTPS endpoint. Cover HMAC validation, timestamp freshness, secret storage, and dashboard testing without registering anything automatically.

output_examples.input: I want to connect ASOScan to Claude but have no API key.
output: If ASOScan tools are unavailable, add the ASOScan connector or plugin from Claude's directory and authorize your account.
An API key is only needed for coding agents without connected ASOScan tools.
After connecting, the assistant can check usage through get_usage.
A 403 indicates that your plan does not include API access.
Review your plan before retrying; creating another key does not resolve a plan restriction.

output_examples.input: Can you create my Teams webhook through the API?
output: Webhook endpoints must be added in the ASOScan dashboard.
Confirm the current Microsoft Workflows setup, then select Microsoft Teams as the ASOScan delivery format.
Enter the workflow destination, choose events, and use Send test to verify delivery.

best_practices: Choose read-only access unless your workflow requires changes, and keep credentials in protected storage rather than shell startup files.
Verify current official instructions before guiding users through Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google, or Apple setup.
Verify connectivity and test webhook delivery before relying on an integration; validate signed event timestamps as well as signatures.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys, webhook signing secrets, or private destination URLs into shared conversations or repositories.
Do not attempt public API webhook registration or assume every account exposes the same integration features.
Do not promise ranking improvements, store listing publication, or ad account setup from this skill.

faq.question: Do I need an API key to use this skill?
faq.answer: No. The setup guidance works without a key. Coding agents without connected ASOScan tools need a key for authenticated API access.

faq.question: Does the skill work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. Connection methods differ: connected assistant tools, Claude Code plugin installation, or API key access for coding agents.

faq.question: What do 401 and 403 responses mean?
faq.answer: A 401 indicates a missing, malformed, unknown, or revoked key. A 403 indicates that the plan does not include API access.

faq.question: Can the skill create webhook endpoints automatically?
faq.answer: No. Add endpoints under Settings and Webhooks in ASOScan, then use Send test to check delivery.

faq.question: Why is a webhook or connection section missing?
faq.answer: Availability depends on plan access, feature flags, and rollout status. A missing section may mean the feature is not enabled for your account.

faq.question: Can connected store accounts publish listing text?
faq.answer: No. Connections read reviews, ratings, and listing text, and allow approved review replies. This skill does not cover ad accounts.
